verdicts.why: In FATWS ep 6 Valentina recruits him as U.S. Agent, but no source names O.X.E. there; the wiki ties O.X.E. to his later missions in Thunderbolts*. The dataset also gives Valentina, Yelena and Taskmaster O.X.E. Group only from Thunderbolts*, so Walker would sit in O.X.E. alone in FATWS. The record stays as it is.

The wiki's 'Finding Structure' section has him join the Army after Eileen Mercer's death and leave it before the suicide-hotline job and the FBI, all before Daredevil S3, where he is already an FBI agent. The Army is backstory.

In DD S2 ep 8 she tells Stick she will fight the Hand without the Chaste and throws him out. In ep 10 Stick sends Jacques Duchamps to kill her as a former Chaste assassin. She holds no group until the Hand resurrects her in The Defenders.

His Army special-ops service (34th Infantry, Damascus) is early-life backstory, and he is already NYPD Officer Simpson when Jessica Jones S1 starts. Rejoining IGH and then leaving it later in S1 stays as it is.

The record is wrong, but the fix is different: Malus shut IGH down in the S2 flashbacks (ep 8/10), years before the present story of Jessica Jones S2, her first title. Under the flashback rule her IGH stage is backstory, so no stage remains (an Independent stage with no group before it says nothing).

Same as Alisa: Malus closes IGH and the clinic in the S2 flashbacks (ep 10), before the present story of Jessica Jones S2, his first title. The wiki lists IGH as former. Under the flashback rule IGH is backstory, so no stage remains.

She quits Trish Talk on air in S2 ep 9 and takes the ZCN job, and in S3 ep 1 ARN TV gives her a show as cover (the wiki lists ZCN and ARN as former). Her own A:st-trish-walker record already tracks ZCN and spells the group 'ARN TV', so that name is used instead of 'ARN'.
He trained in K'un-Lun and was banished centuries ago, then co-founded the Hand. K'un-Lun is backstory, and he is in the Hand throughout.
Her banishment from K'un-Lun and the founding of the Hand are ancient backstory. She leads the Hand throughout The Defenders.
He was banished from K'un-Lun with the other four and co-founded the Hand, all ancient backstory (TD ep 4). He is in the Hand throughout The Defenders.
He was banished from K'un-Lun and co-founded the Hand, all ancient backstory. He is in the Hand throughout The Defenders until he dies.

Iron Fist S2 ('Recruiting Ryhno's Gang', 'Morning of the Mindstorm'): with the Iron Fist he takes in Ryhno's gang, promises to make them warriors and leads them. The wiki lists Ryhno's Gang as a former affiliation, and the name is already in the dataset.
Her VA letter shows she was diagnosed with DID and discharged from the Army before Iron Fist S2, where she works alone as a hire. With the Army stage gone, no group remains.
In Punisher S1 ep 12 he blows up Anvil Headquarters, and the company he built is 'completely destroyed'. He is on the run alone until he forms Jigsaw's Crew in S2.

Despite the wiki's 'Fired from the CIA' heading, in ep 11 Marion James only says he will have no place in the CIA once this is done and that he must retire or be burned. He dies before that happens, and the wiki infobox still lists the CIA as current. This is unsure, so the record stays.

His Army service ended in a PTSD discharge before Punisher S1, so that stage is backstory. But whether the veterans' support group counts as a group is an open owner question (owner_calls.json, A:st-curtis-hoyle), and the dataset doesn't use that name, so I didn't add it. No stage remains.
His SAS service in Helmand was before he moved to the US and Wesley recruited him for Fisk, all before his first title. The wiki lists the SAS as former.

Her S.H.I.E.L.D. service ended with the fall, before S2: Coulson came to bring her back, but HYDRA had already taken her. In S2 she is brainwashed into HYDRA, and her later stay at the Playground was under armed guard before she betrayed them for Ward.

After her Terrigenesis in S2 she is brought to Afterlife, comes to embrace 'my life here ... to help my people' and works as its fortune teller until Jiaying kills her. Afterlife is a group the dataset already uses (Jiaying, Gordon, Lincoln).
The S7 Garrett is a separate altered-timeline version with his own wiki page. This record covers only Season 1 (he dies there), so S7 is not a title the record uses.

After his Terrigenesis (S3 'The Singularity'), Hive's dust makes him 'instantly loyal'. The wiki calls this period 'Under Hive's Control' and says his 'liberation from Hive's influence' came later. That is mind control, which is not a move.

After his corruption arrest he escapes and, in Slingshot, makes a deal with the Watchdogs to help them against Inhumans by selling them a stolen 0-8-4. The wiki lists the Watchdogs as his current affiliation. This matches how the dataset already gives Hellfire, who also made a deal with them, a Watchdogs stage.

In S4 Mace keeps his LMD program going under S.H.I.E.L.D. supervision (the wiki lists S.H.I.E.L.D. as former and his title as consultant). Then, in 'Joining the Watchdogs', he goes to Nadeer and Ivanov's Watchdogs and works from their submarine. Being Hive's hostage in S3 is not a move.

At the Temple of the Forgotten (S6 'The Sign'/'New Life') he stabs May, sends her through as the signal and is 'finally siding with Izel'. He welcomes the Shrike-taken Yo-Yo to 'his and Izel's team'. This is his own true self waking, not mind control, and Izel's Crew is a group the dataset already uses.
